title: Small-batch warmup hit-rate modeling and savings scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight spreadsheet-style modeling doc to show how a small-batch warmup + prefix/KV cache behavior affects token consumption and monthly cost. Goal is to provide a quick ROI calc for prioritization and to capture assumptions clearly for follow-up experiments.

Summary (top line):
- Workload baseline: 6,000,000 requests / month, avg tokens/request = 150, baseline per-token cost = $0.00035.
- Baseline monthly token spend = 900,000,000 tokens -> $315,000/month.
- Modeled impact: prefix/KV cache hits during small-batch warmup save a small number of tokens per request, but at scale that yields measurable monthly savings.

Key modeling assumptions:
- Each prefix cache "hit" saves ~30 tokens (this is a shorthand placeholder; real experiments should measure actual prefix lengths saved).
- Hit-rate scenarios modeled: Low 5%, Medium 20%, High 45%.
- Requests/month fixed at 6M for scenario comparability.
- Per-token unit cost constant across scenarios ($0.00035) — does not model quantization/throughput tiers.
- Implementation effort estimate: 4 engineer-weeks (2 engineers x 2 weeks) for server/runtime + rollout and telemetry.

Quick scenario table (CSV-style):
Scenario,avg_batch_size,prefix_hit_rate,avg_tokens_per_req,month_tokens,month_cost,month_savings,percent_savings,payback_months
Baseline,1,0%,150,900000000,$315000,$0,0.0%,n/a
Low-warmup,2,5%,148.5,891000000,$311850,$3150,1.0%,12.7
Medium-warmup,4,20%,144,864000000,$302400,$12600,4.0%,3.2
High-warmup,8,45%,136.5,819000000,$286650,$28350,9.0%,1.4

Notes on calculations (how to reproduce in a sheet):
- avg_tokens_per_req = baseline_tokens_per_req - (prefix_hit_rate * saved_tokens_per_hit)
  (Example: 150 - 0.20 * 30 = 144)
- month_tokens = requests_per_month * avg_tokens_per_req
- month_cost = month_tokens * per_token_cost
- month_savings = baseline_cost - month_cost
- payback_months = (implementation_cost_usd) / month_savings (implementation_cost_usd = $50,000 in this doc)

Interpretation and sensitivity: 
- Low hit-rate (5%) yields modest savings (~$3k/mo). Not compelling on its own unless the feature opens other optimizations (e.g., larger batch windows, reduced tail latency).
- Medium hit-rate (20%) is the most plausible near-term target for certain chat-like workloads where many requests share short prefixes (e.g., system messages + common user context). At ~$12.6k/mo this reaches ~4 month payback if we assume $50k implementation cost.
- High hit-rate (45%) represents specialized workloads (enterprise templates, heavily templated flows). Savings become significant (~$28k/mo) and justify more aggressive rollout and SLO-backed features.

Breakdowns to add in a follow-up (recommended experiments):
1) Measure actual tokens saved per prefix hit across 3 representative customers/tenants (chat, search, summarization).
2) Collect distribution of prefix lengths and common prefix reuse windows (1s, 5s, 1m).
3) Measure overhead: warmup batching introduces memory/kv cache pressure; quantify latency tail changes and GPU utilization differences.
4) Do end-to-end A/B with telemetry: token counts per request, cache hit events, and per-route cost delta.

Risk notes:
- Overestimating saved tokens per hit is the largest model risk. If saved_tokens_per_hit << 30, payback can exceed 12 months.
- Feature adds complexity to runtime: heartbeats, eviction, and metrics to prevent cache poisoning. Account for SRE time.
- High hit-rate scenarios may require sticky routing or tenant-aware caching which has security/isolation implications (see ENG-9012 discussion).

Implementation suggestions (short):
- Start with an opt-in experiment route group (internal + 2 pilot customers) to collect real hit rates.
- Add per-request telemetry tag for prefix_length and cache_result to measure saved_tokens_per_hit distribution.
- Expose a small dashboard showing tokens/month delta attributable to warmup for pilot customers.

Sample formulas (paste into Google Sheet):
A1 = requests_per_month (6000000)
A2 = baseline_tokens_per_req (150)
A3 = saved_tokens_per_hit (30)
A4 = per_token_cost (0.00035)
A5 = implementation_cost_usd (50000)

For a scenario with hit rate R in cell B1, compute:
avg_tokens_per_req = A2 - (B1 * A3)
month_tokens = A1 * avg_tokens_per_req
month_cost = month_tokens * A4
month_savings = (A1 * A2 * A4) - month_cost
payback_months = A5 / month_savings

Action items / next steps (owner tags):
- [ ] Instrument 3 candidate routes and collect 2 weeks of prefix_length + hit events (owner: Samir) -> ticket JIRA-ENG-5678
- [ ] Run offline script to compute saved_tokens_per_hit distribution per route (owner: Morgan) -> PR #2121
- [ ] Draft rollout plan with SRE for eviction/monitoring (owner: Avery)

Links / references:
- Confluence design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-3452-small-batch-warmup-design
- Pilot ticket: JIRA-ENG-5678
- Experimental PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2121

Notes to reviewers: 
- This is a rough model intended for prioritization discussion. If we decide to move forward, I will convert this into a proper sheet with cells for parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo sim for hit-rate uncertainty, and per-route breakouts.
